scenarios.name: Built-in, with Poki on: the tunnel fails without anyone turning it off (kill the PokiTunnel process: Xcode > Debug > Attach to Process, PokiTunnel, then stop the session). With no hand on the phone, the log shows `local VPN: failed`, `reconnecting in 1 s`, `connected`, `back: 10.7.0.1 answers again; starting the runner now`, and the next agent call works. If it keeps failing, it tries 8 times in about 2 minutes (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 30, 30 s) and stops; then only Enable Local Connection in Setup starts it again. Opening Poki dials nothing (GitHub issue 44).
scenarios.section: 1. Loopback (choose one; no proxy app is required with the built-in connection)
scenarios.detail: 人工真机检查项

scenarios.name: Built-in, with Poki on, the tunnel fails and a different VPN (WireGuard, a work VPN) is turned on before the retry comes: Poki does not dial if it detects that VPN. Setup says `Another VPN appears to be on…`, Home shows it under Needs attention, the log says `another VPN is on; not reconnecting`, and the other VPN stays connected. Detection is best effort: a VPN that sets no proxy, such as Tailscale, may not be detected, so Poki may still dial over it. Turning that VPN off and tapping Enable Local Connection brings the runner back, and the message goes. (The check reads the interfaces iOS has network settings for; confirm it sees a real VPN, and sees none with only Wi-Fi or cellular.)
